subject: Subprocessor scope limitation & evidence plan — Order Form amendment request
messages:
From: procurement@cloudsupply.com
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice of subprocessor change impacting Order Form — CloudSupply

Dylan / team,

Quick heads up: CloudSupply is adding a managed log-archival partner (LogHarbor Inc.) that will handle encrypted backups for our licensed deployments. This is strictly for retention and analytics pipelines; no customer PII is processed at rest. Per our MSA / Order Form flow-down obligations, we are sharing the subprocessor notice and updated vendor list.

Files attached: CloudSupply_Subproc_Notice_20260829.pdf (notice), DPA_Questionnaire_CloudSupply.xlsx (completed by CloudSupply legal).

Can you confirm whether this requires an order-form amendment or any re-consent from your side? If it helps, we can provide a limited-scope APL (access policy) for LogHarbor and a brief KBA table.

Next steps proposed from our side:
- Provide the APL and SOC2 summary by 9/2
- Stand up a short call with your security team if you have open questions

Thanks,
Sara Goodwin
Senior Procurement Manager
CloudSupply, Inc.
procurement@cloudsupply.com

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: procurement@cloudsupply.com (CloudSupply)
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice of subprocessor change impacting Order Form — CloudSupply

Sara — thanks for the notice and the questionnaire. Quick confirmation: we received the docs.

A couple of asks from our side to expedite review:
1) Monica / Laura (cc) — please review limited-scope impact vs Order Form flow-down and confirm whether a signed amendment is required (OrderForm §5.3 and Subprocessor flowdown clause).
2) Sara — please tell us whether LogHarbor will have access to decrypted customer content or only encrypted blobs (the questionnaire seemed ambiguous on key custody).
3) If an amendment is needed, we prefer a narrow, single-paragraph Order Form addendum that:
   - limits LogHarbor access to encrypted backups only
   - binds CloudSupply to notify Redwood within 7 days of any changes to subprocessor access rights
   - requires CloudSupply to provide evidence (SOC2/attestation) within 30 days of request

I attached preliminary redlines (Redlines_Dylan_v1.docx) to give legal a starting point; feel free to decline or propose alternate wording.

I suggest we target a formal response by 9/3 so procurement and security can close this on both sides. If a short sync helps, I'm available 9/1 10–11am PT.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Head of Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: Redlines_Dylan_v1.docx

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, procurement@cloudsupply.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice of subprocessor change impacting Order Form — CloudSupply

Folks — reviewed the supplied questionnaire and Dylan's redline. Summary of legal / security position:

Summary findings:
- LogHarbor as described (credentialed service that stores encrypted backups, no KMS access) is a "subprocessor" under the MSA.
- The proposed change is low to medium risk provided CloudSupply: (a) commits to no key access, (b) adds 7-day notification and (c) provides evidence on request.

Required edits to the Order Form / flowdown (we recommend an amendment rather than a full MSA re-sign):
1) Add an Order Form clause (short addendum) that names LogHarbor as an approved subprocessor and restates the limited access scope.
2) Insert a 7-day notification covenant (CloudSupply must notify Redwood of any subprocessor changes that materially increase access or role).
3) Evidence: require submission of the most recent SOC2 Type II or equivalent attestation for LogHarbor or a written attestation by CloudSupply within 30 days of request.

Operational asks for CloudSupply:
- Confirm whether LogHarbor will ever have access to plaintext (YES/NO). If YES, provide justification and controls.
- If NO, provide KMS architecture diagram (redacted) and the APL you mentioned.

I attached a concise amendment text we can use as an Order Form addendum. If CloudSupply agrees to the narrow language, we can sign an amendment and avoid a broader renegotiation.

Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment stubs: OrderForm_Addendum_Draft.docx

From: sara.goodwin@cloudsupply.com
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice of subprocessor change impacting Order Form — CloudSupply

Monica / Dylan — thanks for the quick review and for the proposed amendment language.

Answers:
- LogHarbor will NOT have KMS or plaintext access — they store encrypted blobs and perform only metadata indexing. We will send the APL and a redacted KMS schematic by EOD 9/1.
- We can accept the proposed 7-day notification requirement and the 30-day attestation evidence clause.

Next steps we suggest:
1) CloudSupply will accept the OrderForm_Addendum_Draft and prepare a countersigned doc for e-signature (we aim to use DocuSign).
2) We will share LogHarbor's SOC2 summary and the APL link by 9/1 as promised.

We'll route the countersigned amendment and a DocuSign envelope link once the APL is uploaded. Please confirm if the clause language from your draft needs any edits before we prepare the DocuSign packet.

Best regards,
Sara Goodwin

CloudSupply, Inc.
